title: Whole-Series Metadata Edit Under MASTER_ONLY Leaves Existing Overrides Unchanged

citations.verbatim_quote: By default, an occurrence inherits all properties from the main object except the start (or due) date-time, which is shifted to match the recurrence id LocalDateTime.  However, individual properties of the occurrence can be modified by a patch or multiple patches.
Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".

The full range of calendar components specified by a recurrence set is referenced by referring to just the "UID" property value corresponding to the calendar component.  The "RECURRENCE-ID" property allows the reference to an individual instance within the recurrence set.

rationale: Unlike JSCalendar (`recurrenceOverrides` patches in RFC 8984 Section 4.3.5), an iCalendar override component is a complete VEVENT or VTODO copy that does not record which individual properties were customized versus inherited from the main component when the override was created. Under `series_edit_override_mode = MASTER_ONLY` (the counterpart to `PROPAGATE_PATCH` in R-L4-003), a whole-series edit (`recurrence_id=None`) updates only the main component and leaves valid standalone `RECURRENCE-ID` override components untouched so per-instance customizations (such as a custom `SUMMARY` or `LOCATION` on one occurrence) are never silently overwritten.
store_implication: Under `series_edit_override_mode = MASTER_ONLY`, when editing a series with `recurrence_id=None`: (1) the main component (`uid == target_uid` and `recurrence_id is None`) is updated in place with the patch and bumped revision metadata (`sequence`, `dtstamp`, `last_modified`); (2) every standalone override component (`uid == target_uid`, `recurrence_id is not None`, no `rrule`/`rdate`) that remains valid after exception handling is preserved without applying the non-schedule metadata patch or incrementing the override's `sequence`/`dtstamp`/`last_modified` (unless the override itself was re-keyed by `SHIFT_WITH_SERIES` in R-L4-009).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Whole-series edit changing `summary` and `location` under `MASTER_ONLY` when an override at May 3 has custom `summary='Guest speaker'`: the main component receives the new `summary` and `location` and increments `sequence`, while the May 3 override retains `summary='Guest speaker'`, its original `location`, and its existing `sequence`.
Component ordering `[override, master]` vs `[master, override]` produces identical results under `MASTER_ONLY` (invariant I-T-009).

scenarios.name: whole_series_metadata_edit_master_only_leaves_override_unchanged
scenarios.description: Under series_edit_override_mode=MASTER_ONLY, editing summary and location on the series updates only the main component and leaves the standalone override component's properties and sequence untouched.

audit_notes: Added explicit rule and scenario covering series_edit_override_mode=MASTER_ONLY.
Verified citations in rfc8984.txt Section 4.3.5 (L1510-L1513), rfc5546.txt Section 4.4.7 (L5862-L5864), and rfc5545.txt Section 3.8.4.7 (L6676-L6680).
